Definition: to load, i.e. impose a burden (or figuratively, infliction)
BiblicalUsage: To load, to impose a burden, and the Bible uses it for the load that breaks and the load that cannot be lifted. Joseph's brothers rent their clothes and laded every man his ass and returned to the city, the silver cup found in Benjamin's sack. And Jerusalem will be made a burdensome stone for all people, that all that burden themselves with it shall be cut in pieces.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for loading carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two burdens, that the brothers carried their guilt home on their asses and the nations will cut themselves trying to lift Jerusalem.
